question: Access to healthcare is a fundamental right. However, according to the 2024 data1 recently published by Eurostat, Greece has the highest share of obstacles to medical care in the EU. In Greece, 21.9 % of citizens over the age of 16 said that they failed to receive the care they needed, while the corresponding figure for the EU as a whole stood at 3.6 %.

2 Cost and geographical distance to health facilities were listed among the main obstacles.3 What is particularly worrying is that more than 30 % of people at risk of poverty reported unmet needs, suggesting strong social inequalities. Given the above, can the Commission say: 1.
What is the Commission’s view of Greece ranking lowest in the 2024 data?
What measures will it take to ensure that economically disadvantaged or geographically isolated citizens are not deprived of access to basic medical services?
Will it support Greece with targeted programmes to strengthen primary care and reduce waiting lists and geographical barriers?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.11.2025) In 2020, 2022 and 2023, Greece has received country-specific recommendations under the European Semester to ensure adequate and equal access to healthcare, notably for primary healthcare. In the 2025 Semester, Greece also received a recommendation to increase the effectiveness and efficiency of the social protection system to address poverty and social exclusion.

Without prejudice to national responsibilities for the Greek health system (Article 168(7) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union), the current grant component of the Greek Recovery and Resilience plan (RRP) includes measures with estimated costs equal to EUR 1,558 million to improve resilience, accessibility and sustainability of the healthcare system.

One important measure concerns a reform of the primary health care system, including increased curricula in family medicine and renovation of primary healthcare health centres. An additional EUR 276 million (EU allocation) has been allocated under the European Regional Development Fund to co-finance infrastructure and equipment at all levels of care in the Greek national health system.

Moreover, around EUR 250 million are allocated by the European Social Fund Plus towards investments to improve the accessibility and effectiveness of Greek primary healthcare services. The above measures are expected to support health services in Greece, including equal access, efficiency and social cohesion, also by strengthening primary care.
